rationale: Requires intermediate representations to be delivered without modification, which is data integrity.
Validating a group signature confirms the message origin (registered airline) and implies detection of alteration.
Encrypts radar records so unauthorised readers cannot interpret them, which is confidentiality.
Restricts modification of bookmarks and form entries to the profile owner who has been verified in the session.
Admits a customer only after identifier and credential are validated, which is authentication.
Verifies claimed identity via digital certificate validation at login.
Verifies analyst credentials against registered records before access, which is authentication.
A cryptographic signature on load records is used to detect later changes to the amount, which is integrity.
Credential reset is delivered to the registered email address, an identity-verification step for credential recovery.
Requires proprietary parameters to be received under encryption, protecting them from disclosure.
Checksum verification refuses to compile if components were modified, which is integrity of programs.
Protects encryption keys in a hardware-backed store so other applications cannot read them.
Reacts to a replayed licence grant, which is a replay attack.
Hash on the stored balance is checked and operation is refused on mismatch, which is tamper detection.
Validates metadata ranges and rejects duplicate identifiers, which is validation of data accuracy and coherence.
Encrypted transport so intermediaries cannot read submitted values.
Hash comparison blocks payment when the payslip batch differs, which is alteration detection.
Per-module control over who may view and who may alter content covers both read and modify restrictions.
Detects and blocks script injection attacks while keeping simulations operating, which is resistance.
Strips user names, paths and source snippets from crash reports to avoid disclosure to support staff.
Ensures debit and credit amounts match and rejects inconsistent entries, which is data consistency integrity.
Purges intermediate data so later users cannot read it, which is protection against disclosure.
Dashboard access depends on the controller confirming the resident's identity.
Recomputes ledger checksums and retains the rolled-back entry unchanged, which supports data integrity.
Public-key encryption conceals session keys during distribution, which is confidentiality.
Rejects repeated crafted inputs meant to exhaust the service and alerts the administrator, which is attack resistance.
Requires proving ownership of the profile with a verified credential before restore, which is authentication.
Validates clinical entry accuracy and rejects injected or manipulated entries that try to bypass checks.
Requires the correct PIN before authorising payment, which is authentication.
Responds to an attacker's replay of an authentication assertion by terminating the session, which is attack resistance.
Keyed authentication tag verification detects altered commands and verifies they come from the paired hub.
Requires sign-in with an enrolled account and valid credential, which is authentication.
Discards stale-timestamp commands to prevent replay of recorded commands, which is replay-attack resistance.
Informs whether a verifiable source stamp confirms the data provider's identity, which concerns origin authenticity.
Erases personal and payment data from temporary storage after timeout, protecting privacy.
Digest comparison detects modified source files before compilation, which is integrity.
Encrypts payloads so only the paired mobile app can read them, which is confidentiality.
Prevents partially updated records and restricts modification to users with an edit role.
Cryptographic checksum on the balance detects corruption or tampering, which is integrity.
